shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Cross-level combat, senses, NPC travel, CE bridge (experimental), climb animations, wall risers, research-gated links, Perspective Shift + Toggleable Overlays support, and global click-through so open air is never a click target. Windows 12+13 are SHIPPED. Window 14 is building Combat Extended compat for manned weapons.

**NOTE TO SELF:** running spec, not a changelog. §0 handover; §1-19 architecture; §20 compat; §21-29 bug records; §30 SUPERSEDED by §62; §31 publishing + GIT; §32-40 records; §41-44 combat/senses/travel/CE; §51 Celestial Lighting; §52 field-report round 2; §53 arrival/landing; §54 structure fit; §55 exit grid; §56 Geological Landforms; §57 stale decoration window; §58 relocated-structure fog; §59 forbid-aware islands; §60 area-linear vanilla systems; §61 camera-mod coexistence; §62 utility COLUMN rework + §62.N; §63 stairs permission; §64 cross-level shadow depth; §65 forbidden mirroring; §66 aim/wild-miss/aim-pie; §67 boulder extrusion; §68 KCSG/VFEM2; §69 stair temperature; §70 band flora legality + §70.B (OPEN); §71 Smooth Terrain (RESOLVED; report awaiting paste); §72 link gizmos; §73 transit animations (SUPERSEDED); §74 blueprint art; §75 wall risers; §76 Perspective Shift; §77 motion study + §77c art defects; §78 pre-hop delay + climb grammar; §79 Toggleable Overlays; §80 research gating; §81 multiple-levels checkbox; §82 cross-level targeting; §83 band-aware overlays; §84 cross-level AI jumping; §85 open-side arrivals + 1x2 staircase; §86 PS return-to-character; §87 GLOBAL click-through opt-out; **§88 CE manned weapons (WINDOW 14, IN PROGRESS)**; **§89 stacked-pawn stall (DIAGNOSED, INSTRUMENTED, NOT FIXED)**; **§90 disembark tile for stairs orders (SHIPPED-quality, FIELD-VERIFIED)**. Keep every ⚠. # As above, So below II (V2) > **⚠⚠ V1 SOURCE IS NOT GONE. DATED SOURCE BACKUPS LIVE AT `D:\Rimworld\As above, So below\\Source\`** (ten snapshots, newest `20260726-154207`). `Source/` only - no Defs, no Textures. **When a V2 feature has a V1 ancestor, READ THE V1 FILE FIRST.** Confirmed useful: `Source/Stairs/ClimbAnimation.cs` (§78d). Tool boundary: `read` refuses that path, `bash`/`grep`/`sed` reach it fine. # 0. START HERE **CURRENT PHASE: WINDOW 15, BUILD MODE. §88 (CE MANNED WEAPONS) IS THE ACTIVE WORK.** **✅ WINDOWS 12, 13 AND 14 ARE SHIPPED** to Workshop 3776015553. Windows 12+13 on 2026-08-29 (`b182988`, content `6485daf`); **window 14 (§90 only) the same day**, prep commit **`00111c4`**. Change notes are `docs/UPDATE_NOTES.txt`, REWRITTEN each release - window 14's is the one-item stairs note, and window 13's text is gone unless recovered from git history. **THE WORKSPACE DLL IS A DEBUG BUILD - THE NORMAL STATE** (post-publish restore verified by decompiling: `ABV2Debug.LogTransit == true`). §85.16 transit tracing is ON, which is why a test run fills the bridge with `TRANSIT:` warnings; that is expected and reaches no player. **⚠⚠ THE WORKSHOP SMOKE TEST STILL HAS NEVER BEEN DONE.** SIXTEEN windows, every verification against the WORKSPACE copy. Nobody has subscribed to item 3776015553 and loaded THAT copy. Deferred again at publish time by explicit choice. A file that exists locally but never uploaded would still pass every check this project has ever made. **PUBLISH PROCEDURE IS PROVEN AND REPEATABLE (windows 13 AND 14).** ⚠ THE WINDOW-14 RUN ADDED ONE FINDING: **the source edits were already committed by MODMIXER AUTOSAVE** (`autosave ` commits), so `git diff HEAD` showed only the dll and looked alarmingly empty. Autosave means work is never lost, but it also means a hand-written "publish prep" commit may contain almost nothing. Check `git log`, not just `git status`. Staging dir `workspace/_publish-staging//`, six moves out, contraband scan, publish, six moves back, rebuild, commit "shipped". ⚠ **VERIFY THE BUILD CONFIG BY DECOMPILING, NOT BY READING THE BUILD OUTPUT** - `dotnet build -c Release` printed "up-to-date" in 0.73s and looked like a no-op; only `ABV2Debug.LogTransit == false` in the actual binary proves it. ⚠ **CHECK `LoadFolders.xml` SURVIVED THE STRIP** - its `
  • /
    • ` root entry is load-bearing, and a mod that lost it uploads as zero defs, zero textures, no assembly while the file list still looks plausible. **⚠ OPEN, NOT URGENT:** **§85 TAG PASS** (`Tools/LinkApproachTagger.html`; until the export is pasted back, all 24 sprites run on derived defaults). **§85.9 ART** - `AB_StairsUp_east/west` are the tall flight exported at a ~15-20 degree ROTATION; redraw or one-rotating-graphic, user's call. **FINAL riser art** (Gemini PAUSED r5; ⚠ REWRITE prompts to the REAL palette - NO copper: power=steel+blue+hazard, pipe=pale+red valve, climate=ice+louver+orange, data=black+purple+cyan). **§77c ART** - grand staircase east/west unrotated; user's domain. **ABOUT.XML DESCRIPTION IS STALE** (no research gating, off switch, AI jumping or click-through) and **`About/Preview.png` is from Aug 5** - USER'S COPY, flagged not fixed. **`About/known-issues.json`** unchanged since window 8. **⚠ SHIPPED KNOWINGLY UNVERIFIED:** §85's flipped up-link `approachCells` (stairs n/e/w, grand-up x4, ladder-up x4) and §85.23's float-menu verbs (w13); §62.N, §70 (w8); §62.M, §66c, §66e (w7). **⚠ USER WORKING RULES:** (1) NEVER source design ideas from other mods unless asked - scans COMPAT ONLY. **V1 is OUR OWN prior work and is exempt.** (2) Building art = USER via Nano Banana kits. (3) About.xml description = USER's copy. (4) N mockups = N CHOICES. **What this mod is.** Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`, banded along +z. Priorities: visual clarity from above, performance, vanilla parity. **⚠⚠ THE SEVENTY-THREE RULES:** 1. CLAMP AT SELECTION. 2. NEVER PATCH `TryRebuildDirtyRegionsAndRooms`. 3. REGION CONNECTIVITY IS MORE OPTIMISTIC THAN THE PATHFINDER: flood CELLS. 4. COUNT EMITTERS/POPULATIONS/ENGINE STACKS. 5 (§48): A `Touch` TARGET IS USUALLY UNWALKABLE. 6 (§49): A VANILLA HELPER CAN BE A NO-OP INSTEAD OF AN ERROR. 7 (§52): THE CARVE IS NOT THE LAST WORD. 8 (§52.6): A LOAD-TIME REPAIR PASS MUST NEVER RE-CREATE WHAT THE PLAYER DELIBERATELY REMOVED. 9 (§53): SOME MISPLACEMENTS ARE NOT VISIBLE IN THE CELL. 10 (§54): A STRUCTURE IS NOT A CELL. 11 (§55): A CELL-LEVEL VERDICT CANNOT AUTHORIZE A PAWN-LEVEL ACTION. 12 (§56a): A FOREIGN MOD'S MAP-SIZE SNAPSHOT IS AN INPUT YOU CAN CORRECT. 13 (§56g): NEVER COPY A GRID YOU DID NOT WATCH BEING WRITTEN. 14 (§56m): BEFORE RELOCATING DATA, ASK WHAT IS ALREADY AT THE DESTINATION. 15 (§57i): ASSERT ALWAYS, NARRATE ON REQUEST. 16 (§56o): COUNT THE FOREIGN MOD'S WRITE PATHS. 17 (§56q): A PASSING RUN THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE THE FAILURE IS NOT A FIX - **and its publish-time twin: A BUILD MESSAGE IS NOT PROOF THE RIGHT THING WAS BUILT; decompile the binary.** 18 (§57a): **NEVER EXONERATE A SUSPECT ON ONE CLEAN SAMPLE** - grep version at rule 54. 19 (§57f): `TicksGame` RESTARTS AT 0 EVERY NEW GAME. 20 (§57g): MOVING WORK EARLIER TURNS ON EVERY "IS THIS MAP READY" GATE. 21 (§58): THE PARALLEL GRIDS DO NOT TRAVEL WITH THE CONTENT. 22 (§59): A DERIVED GRID HAS NO PAWN IN IT. 23 (§60): AUDIT THE WEIGHTING, NOT THE SYMBOL. 24 (§61a): CLAMPING A VALUE WITHOUT CLAMPING ITS TARGET BUILDS AN OSCILLATOR. 25 (§61b): A POSTFIX ON `Update` IS AFTER THE OBJECT WAS ALREADY POSITIONED. 26 (§61f): EVERY READ OF THE MAP THE PLAYER CAN REACH MUST PASS THE RENDERER'S "IS IT DRAWN" GATE - selectable is drawable, and so is **highlightable** (§83). 27 (§62c): PREFER SPAWN/DESPAWN OVER FLICK. 28 (§63a): A PERMANENT FICTION INSTALLED FOR ONE SUBSYSTEM IS READ AS FACT BY EVERY OTHER ONE. 29 (§0b): REPORT OUTCOMES, NOT INTENTIONS. 30 (§66d): A FELT DURATION IS A CHAIN, NOT A NUMBER. 31 (§66f): MAKE THE GUARD SAY WHICH CLAUSE DECLINED. 32 (§69a): TURNING OFF A TICK TURNS OFF EVERY SERVICE THAT RODE ON IT. 33 (§62k): A FILTER THAT CAN REJECT EVERYTHING MUST SAY SO. 34 (§62l): AN INVISIBLE THING IS ABSENT FROM EVERY SECTION LAYER. 35 (§62n): A CLONED FOREIGN DEF MADE VISIBLE IS IN NONE OF THE HOST'S OWN LOOKUPS. 36 (§70a): RUN VANILLA'S OWN LEGALITY PREDICATE. 37 (§71a): NAME THE ENFORCEMENT POINT BEFORE NAMING THE SYMPTOM. 38 (§73): WHEN A SPRITE MUST APPEAR AWAY FROM ITS THING'S POSITION, OWN THE DRAW - and §84.8's other half. 39 (§76): WINNING THE LAST WRITE DOES NOT SETTLE A DISAGREEMENT ABOUT THE TARGET. 40 (§75.h): A TRIPWIRE THAT FIRES BEFORE THE OBSERVER ATTACHES IS NOT A TRIPWIRE. 41 (§77a): A STRUCT FIELD YOU NEVER SET IS A FEATURE YOU NEVER SHIPPED. 42 (§77b): THE DIRECTION A MOTION READS AS IS A PROPERTY OF THE THING, NOT OF THE ARRIVAL. 43 (§78): **DEFER THE MOVE, NEVER THE DECISION.** 44 (§78b): AN OFFSET APPLIED WHOLE ON FRAME ONE IS A TELEPORT. 45 (§78d): **A DIRECTION OF TRAVEL IS NOT A DIRECTION OF ELEVATION.** 46 (§78d): **NON-UNIFORM SCALE x ROTATION = SHEAR.** 47 (§79): **A FOREIGN MOD'S CACHED CURSOR CELL IS AN ASSUMPTION ABOUT COORDINATE SPACE.** 48 (§81a): **A WRITE THAT IS READ BACK BY ITS OWN CALLER IS NOT A WRITE.** 49 (§0c): **A TEST THAT PROVES FEATURE A SAYS NOTHING ABOUT FEATURE B.** 50 (§82a): **TWO OF OUR OWN PATCHES ON ONE VANILLA METHOD CANCEL SILENTLY.** GREP OUR OWN `[HarmonyPatch]` LIST FIRST. 51 (§82b): **A FACTORY HAS USUALLY CONSUMED ITS INPUT BY THE TIME THE POSTFIX RUNS.** 52 (§83a): **AN OVERLAY MUST ASK THE SAME QUESTION THE CLICK WILL ASK, AND IT MUST NOT BE A QUESTION THAT WRITES.** 53 (§83c): **A PREDICATE PASSED IN IS CLOSED OVER THE ARGUMENTS THE CALLER ALREADY HAS.** 54 (§84a): **A CLEAN GREP IS NOT AN ABSENCE - SEARCH FOR THE CAPABILITY, NOT THE TYPE NAME.** 55 (§84.3): **"AFTER THE DUTY HAD ITS TURN" INCLUDES A FALLBACK JOB YOU WOULD NEVER CALL A REAL ONE.** 56 (§84.5): **WHEN YOU RANK CANDIDATES BY ONE COST AND FILTER THEM BY ANOTHER, THE RANKING FINDS THE FILTER'S BLIND SPOT.** 57 (§85a): **WHEN TWO SUBSYSTEMS EACH ANSWER "WHICH SIDE OF THIS THING", ONE OF THEM IS ABOUT TO BE WRONG.** 58 (§85b): **A PROPERTY OF THE ART CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THE DEF.** 59 (§85.8): **`size` MUST BE MEASURED FROM THE DRAWING, NOT COPIED FROM `drawSize`.** 60 (§85.9): **MEASURE THE PIXELS; A DRAW OFFSET AND AN ART-OFFSET TABLE ARE THE SAME NUMBER TWICE.** 61 (§85c): **A COLOURED VERSION OF A GRAPHIC IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT, AND VANILLA HARD-CODES ITS TYPE.** 62 (§85d): **A TABLE OF FINISHED ANSWERS ROTS; STORE ONLY WHAT NOTHING ELSE OWNS AND DERIVE THE REST.** 63 (§85.14): **MEASURE A PATIENCE FROM THE EVENT IT NAMES.** 64 (§85.16): **A DIAGNOSTIC THAT IS OFF BY DEFAULT IS A DIAGNOSTIC THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** 65 (§85.17): **WHEN A DERIVED RULE IS RIGHT THREE TIMES OUT OF FOUR, THE FOURTH IS A DEFECTIVE INPUT.** 66 (§85.19): **A DESTINATION CELL DOES NOT CONSTRAIN THE SIDE IT IS ENTERED FROM.** 67 (§85.20): **AN EARLY RETURN THAT PRESERVES STATE MUST ASK WHO SENT THE NEW ORDER.** 68 (§85.22): **WHEN THE SAME 'EXCEPTION' IS REPORTED TWICE ON ONE DEF, IT IS THE DEF'S RULE, NOT TWO EXCEPTIONS.** 69 (§86a): **WHEN YOU SUSPEND A FOREIGN MOD'S DRIVER, YOU INHERIT EVERY REQUEST THAT DRIVER SERVED.** A UI control can be nothing but a cleared field whose only consumer is the loop you switched off. Enumerate what READS the state you neutralised, not just what writes it. 70 (§87a): **AN OPT-IN CORRECTION APPLIED AT N CONSUMERS IS A DEFAULT APPLIED AT THE WRONG LAYER.** Correct it at the source and enumerate the EXCEPTIONS - that list is finite, auditable and self-reporting; the consumer list grows silently forever. 71 (§89): **A PROBE THAT ASKS FOR "THE" OCCUPANT CANNOT SEE A STACK.** `GetFirstPawn` + "is it me?" reports `none` for the one arrangement that matters. When a diagnostic exonerates a cell, check whether it COUNTED or merely peeked. 72 (§90): **A DESTINATION THAT NAMES A BUILDING OUTLIVES EVERY CORRECTION MADE TO THE ARRIVAL.** Placing a pawn well is undone one tick later by a live job still pointing at the building it was placed beside. When you fix WHERE something lands, go and read what ORDERED it there. 73 (§89): **A PROBE THAT COMPUTES ITS OWN ANSWER IS NOT READING THE SUBJECT'S.** The stuck watchdog printed `path=FOUND (21 nodes)` from its own `FindPathNow` call - which proves a route EXISTS, never that the pather HOLDS one - and that one word sent us hunting an obstruction for five sightings. When a diagnostic reports on someone else's state, read THEIR field or say plainly whose answer it is. --- # WINDOW 15 LEDGER (open) 1. **§88 CE MANNED WEAPONS - ACTIVE WORK, NOT STARTED.** Plan and findings in §88. Window 14 spent itself on §90 and a publish instead. 2. **⚠⚠ THE WORKSHOP SMOKE TEST.** Subscribe to 3776015553, load THAT copy. Still never done. 3. **§89 STALL - THE STACK HYPOTHESIS IS DEAD (run #397) AND FURTHER INSTRUMENTATION IS DECLINED BY THE USER.** Do not add watchdog fields without asking. If it is ever reopened, the two unread clauses are named in §89b. 4. **⚠ §85 SHIPPED-UNVERIFIED:** the flipped up-link `approachCells` and §85.23's float-menu verbs went out untested. Watch for reports. 5. **⚠ `CarveLanding` leaves the front tile unstandable inside fresh pockets** (3 sightings). 6. **⚠ §83 SCOPE GAPS (rule 49):** AoE circle, **turret ring from another band (also §88 PART 4)**, truncation cap. 7. **⚠ §84 SCOPE GAPS (rule 49):** PART A (mech giver repair), PART C (escape clamp). 8. **⚠ OTHER ABILITY GIVERS UNAUDITED (rule 54):** `JobGiver_AISkipToJobTarget`, `JobGiver_AIAbilityFight`, `JobGiver_AICastAbility`, `JobGiver_AICastAbilityOnSelf`. 9. **⚠ TOGGLEABLE OVERLAYS NOT RE-TESTED SINCE §78,** and §87 now moves the mouse itself. §79.1 reads TO's cached cursor from their own ray so it should be untouched - UNVERIFIED. (PS *was* re-verified in #395.) 10. **§87 FOLLOW-UP:** `MultiPawnGotoController.ProcessInputEvents` is suppressed to preserve §33f; letting `end` descend is probably an improvement, deliberately untried. 11. **§78 FOLLOW-ONS:** delete retired ghost stubs; AnimationDef pipeline port (OFFERED, NOT ACCEPTED); hostiles skipping the hold. 12. **⚠ FOREIGN PRINT-PATH AUDIT.** RimIOT and Eccentric Tech never decompiled. Rule 18. 13. **§62.N formal line. §70 field verify (§70.B OPEN). §71 upstream report. §75/§76/§79.4/§80.4 residue. §82/§83/§84.10/§85.7 residue. §77 mockup D. §64; §65; §61; §60/59/58/55/54/53; §56.1; DATA network thin; DCH `Hosts` row.** 14. **§90 DISEMBARK TILE - DONE, FIELD-VERIFIED, SHIPPED.** Nothing outstanding. Its two untested branches (elevator fallback, walled-in front tile) are reasoned-only and now live on the Workshop. **⚠ TEST-LOOP NOTES:** palette pins resolve during map init - use the Debug Actions MENU for `PlayingOnMap` actions. **PS runs and the §81 dialog need `quicktest=false`, and PS must be passed as `companionMods: ["ferny.PerspectiveShift"]` in an isolated run or it will not load.** **A CE run needs CE + its dependency chain the same way, or `isolated:false`.** **Startup warnings never reach the bridge.** **`build_mod` builds DEBUG** (so `LogTransit` is ON). **⚠ CHECK `Mod_50b4332c2547_ABMod.xml` IN THE TEST SAVEDATA BEFORE A BANDED RUN** (absent `multiLevel` = TRUE). **⚠ SKY BANDS ARE THE CHEAPEST SEE-THROUGH TEST RIG**; the INVERSE rig is how upward gets tested. **⚠ `AB2: place stairs down here` SPAWNS AT Rot4.North.** **⚠⚠ `Log.Message` NEVER REACHES THE BRIDGE, BUT `Player.log` IS READABLE FROM HERE** - `C:\Users\Astryl\AppData\LocalLow\Ludeon Studios\RimWorld by Ludeon Studios\Player.log`, and it does NOT move for an isolated savedata run. **⚠ ART IS MEASURABLE FROM HERE: `Tools/MeasureSprites.ps1`.** ⚠ Long `newText` blocks in the edit tool have truncated mid-string SIX times; write a temp file INSIDE THE MOD FOLDER and splice with python. **⚠ KNOWN-BENIGN FOREIGN NOISE:** VFEM2 TorchWallLamp MakeThing error; Rimefeller `discord.dds` `f2fab05fc732a605`; Rimefeller `CompOilDerrick.setfull` NRE (`#fc35ef297211de6b`). NONE ARE OURS. --- # 1-30 — unchanged. # 31 PUBLISHING — `docs/PUBLISH_CHECKLIST.md` IS AUTHORITATIVE Strip = SIX moves (`Source/`, `Tools/`, `docs/`, `.git/`, `mockups/`, `.gitignore`) to a staging dir OUTSIDE `Mods/`; the utility pushes FILES + PREVIEW ONLY, so change notes and description go into the Steam **web** editor by hand. Commit and push BEFORE the strip. **⚠ `.gitignore` travels with `.git/`.** Proven window-13 run: release build → **decompile to prove it IS Release** → log-hygiene grep → metadata check → write `UPDATE_NOTES.txt` and grep it for em-dashes (house rule) → commit and push → strip with a loop that PRINTS each move and says ABSENT for anything missing → contraband `find` (`obj`/`bin`/`*.pdb`/`*.csproj`/`*.cs`/`0Harmony.dll`) → **confirm `LoadFolders.xml` survived** → publish → restore with the same loop → rebuild to prove the restore lost nothing → commit "shipped". Record the staging path in §0 while stripped. # 32-87 — unchanged (see the index line at the top). §86 and §87 SHIPPED, both field-verified #395. # 88. COMBAT EXTENDED — MANNED WEAPONS ("STATIONARY MACHINE GUNS") — **WINDOW 14, IN PROGRESS** User picked the MANNED case specifically (a pawn operating a stationary gun), not CE turrets in general. **88.1 WHAT ALREADY WORKS.** The four §44 seams key on `Verb_LaunchProjectileCE`, `ShiftVecReport`, `ShiftTarget` and `ProjectileCE.Launch`, all of which a manned CE gun uses - shot legality, aim space, projectile origin and the high-ground suppression model are already band-aware for it. **⚠⚠ 88a WHAT DOES NOT, FROM DECOMPILING `CombatExtended.Building_TurretGunCE`.** It derives from `Building_Turret`, NOT `Building_TurretGun`, so `Patch_BuildingTurretGun_ABBandLocalForcedTarget` never runs on it. And `CanSetForcedTarget => mannableComp != null && PlayerControlled` - **in CE, force-targeting exists ONLY on MANNABLE turrets**, so the forced-target path IS the manned-gun path, which is what makes PART 1 the whole user-facing feature rather than a detail. Its `OrderAttack` does the raw `(targ.Cell - Position).LengthHorizontal` against `minRange` and `range`: §1's slicing rule, wrong in both directions across bands. **88.2 THE PLAN.** - **PART 1 (essential): `Building_TurretGunCE.OrderAttack`.** House pattern: a reflection-only, `Prepare()`-shape-validated prefix handling ONLY the cross-band case - re-run the two limits band-locally via `ABCombatV2.TrySolve`, then replicate CE's short tail (`forcedTarget = targ`, `TryStartShootSomething(false)`, the holdFire message). Same-band orders fall through to CE untouched. ⚠ REJECTED: a transpiler (fragile to write blind); and translating `targ` for the duration of CE's own body (CE sets `currentTargetInt` inside it, so the gun would fire at the translated cell for a tick). - **PART 2: `CompFireArc.WithinFireArc`** - both `OrderAttack` and `IsValidTarget` gate on it and the angle is raw geometry. Only defs carrying the comp. - **PART 3: acquisition - VERIFY, DON'T ASSUME (rule 54).** `TargSearcher()` returns the MANNING PAWN when manned; a non-`NonSnap` gun then goes through vanilla `AttackTargetFinder.BestShootTargetFromCurrentPosition`, which our §42 postfix covers. Believed fine, unproven. ⚠ A def carrying `NonSnapTurretExtension` uses CE's own `NonSnapAttackTargetFinder` and is NOT covered. - **PART 4: `DrawRangeRings`** - `GenDraw.DrawRadiusRing(Position, range)`, i.e. §83.7's "turret ring from another band" gap, now with an owner. **⚠ 88.3 TESTING IS THE EXPENSIVE PART.** Needs `isolated:false` or a `companionMods` launch with CE and its dependency chain - heavier and noisier than any window-12/13 test. CE is installed at load order 38, packageId `CETeam.CombatExtended`. # 89. THE STACKED-PAWN STALL — **DIAGNOSED, INSTRUMENTED, NOT FIXED** Five sightings across four runs (Rogue x2, Rynyk, Hunin, Jay). Signature always identical: `moving=True`, `path=FOUND`, `CanReach=True`, destination stable, **not advancing**. First four `GotoWander`; #395's was a player-ordered `Goto`, which rules out anything wander-specific. **⚠⚠ 89a THE TELL, AND OUR PROBE WAS BLIND TO IT (rule 71).** #395 logged `Jay at (63,0,458) ... nextCell=(63,0,458) ... occupant=none`. **The pather's next cell is the cell the pawn already stands on.** The old probe did `next.GetFirstPawn(map)` then discarded the answer when it was the watched pawn - so for TWO PAWNS ON ONE CELL it printed `none`, and the report read "nothing is in the way" while the pawn was in its own way. **THE VANILLA MECHANISM IS AN INFINITE EARLY RETURN.** `Pawn_PathFollower.PatherTick` opens with `if (WillCollideWithPawnAt(pawn.Position, forceOnlyStanding: true, useId: true))`; it tries `CellFinder.TryFindBestPawnStandCell`, and on failure stamps `failedToFindCloseUnoccupiedCellTicks`, after which `FailedToFindCloseUnoccupiedCellRecently()` (a 100-tick window) makes PatherTick **return before any movement code** every tick. `moving` stays true, the path stays found, `nextCell` never leaves `Position`. **INSTRUMENTED IN WINDOW 13, NOT FIXED.** `ABStuckWatchdog` now (a) COUNTS every pawn on the cell, self included and labelled, each tagged moving/idle and **`TRANSIT`** if `ABWormholePather.HasPending`; (b) invokes vanilla's own `WillCollideWithPawnAt` by reflection rather than reimplementing it - **the `useId` tie-break decides WHICH of two co-located pawns yields, and guessing it wrong inverts the answer on exactly this case**; (c) reads `failedToFindCloseUnoccupiedCellTicks` with vanilla's 100-tick window copied verbatim; (d) emits a `SELF-STACK` verdict ahead of `BLOCKED`; (e) warns once (rule 33) if either private member fails to bind, because a silent degrade returns the exact wording that hid this for five sightings. **⚠⚠ 89b THE SIXTH SIGHTING KILLED THE HYPOTHESIS (run #397).** Baldwin, `GotoWander`, 214 ticks still, `moving=True`, `path=FOUND`, dest stable - and the new instrumentation reported **`pawnsHere=1 [SELF(moving)]`, `collidesHere=False`, `unstickGaveUp=no`**. There is no co-occupant and vanilla's own `WillCollideWithPawnAt` says no collision, so the `FailedToFindCloseUnoccupiedCellRecently` early return that §89 spent a window building for **cannot be what is happening here**. Window 13 nearly convicted on a hypothesis; its own instrument acquitted it. Rule 18 earns its keep in both directions. **WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT.** With `collidesHere=False` vanilla's 1.6 `PatherTick` is in the `else` branch, where exactly three early returns leave `moving=True` and never reach movement code: 1. `pawn.stances.FullBodyBusy` - **unread by the watchdog**; 2. `moving && curPath == null` - the wait on 1.6's ASYNC `curPathRequest`; **also unread**; 3. `moving && WillCollideNextCell` - excluded, `nextCell` is the pawn's own cell. `nextCell == Position` is precisely the state while `curPath` is null and `SetupMoveIntoNextCell` has never run, so (2) fits every observed field without strain. **NOT A CONVICTION.** **⚠⚠ AND THE TRAP THAT SENT US WRONG (rule 73): `path=FOUND (21 nodes)` IS THE WATCHDOG'S OWN `map.pathFinder.FindPathNow` PROBE, NOT `curPath`.** It proves a route exists; it says nothing about whether the pather holds one. Read `Report()` before trusting that field again. The `BLOCKED` verdict string is likewise now known to overstate - it asserts "movement is obstructed" on a cell where nothing is obstructing. **⚠ OUR `PathFinder.PushRequest` PREFIX WAS CHECKED AND FELL THROUGH.** It only resolves CROSS-BAND requests; Baldwin's start and destination were both band 1. Not exoneration, not a lead. **⚠⚠ USER DECISION, RUN #397: NO FURTHER INSTRUMENTATION.** "We don't need to fill users logs with spam." Do not add watchdog fields without asking again. (For the record, the concern is already structurally covered: `ABStuckWatchdog.Tick` opens with `if (!ABV2Debug.LogTransit) return;` and `LogTransit` is `#if DEBUG`, so no Release build has ever written a `V2 STUCK` line to a player's log.) The stall remains OPEN, UNDIAGNOSED and rare. # 90. THE STAIRS ORDER LANDED THE PAWN ON THE STAIRCASE - **FIXED IN WORKSPACE, NOT FIELD-TESTED** Field report: "when a pawn finishes its journey across levels via stairs or ladders, they should path off the building, not go to the building cell", called out as especially visible under Perspective Shift - a pawn standing on the link is drawn INSIDE the stair art instead of beside it. **⚠⚠ 90a THE ARRIVAL WAS NEVER THE BUG; THE ORDER WAS.** §85's `LandingCell`/`ApproachLanding` have set transiting pawns down on the tile in front of the far opening for two windows and did so correctly here. `FloatMenuOptionProvider_ABStairsTravel` then handed the pawn a `JobDefOf.Goto` aimed at **`far.Position`** - a cell INSIDE the far link's own footprint. The pawn crossed, landed on the front tile, and its still-live job immediately walked it BACK ONTO the staircase and parked it. Two subsystems, one journey, opposite opinions about where it ends; the later one wins and it was the one nobody had revisited. Hence rule 72. **THE FIX.** `ABLinkApproach.DisembarkCell(link)` - new, deliberately sited next to `TryGet` so the order site and the landing site read the SAME per-def approach table (rule 57) instead of each deriving an open edge. Returns the tagged `outside` tile validated for in-bounds, `Standable` and same-band; `IntVec3.Invalid` otherwise. `ABStairsOrders` aims its Goto there and falls back to `far.Position` when it is Invalid. - **Standable, not Walkable** - the cell is OFF the footprint, so walkable-but-not-standable out here is somebody ELSE's doorway (same distinction `ApproachLanding` and `EntryCellFor` draw, opposite ways, for the same reason). - **Same-band is not redundant** - a link flush against a band edge has a neighbour cell that is a different LEVEL sharing an x/z edge. - **Occupancy is not tested, on purpose and twice over**: `Standable` ignores pawns by design, and who stands there at ORDER time says nothing about who stands there on arrival, possibly hundreds of ticks later. A blocked tile makes a queue (§85.19), which is correct for a staircase. - **ELEVATORS ARE UNCHANGED BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THAT IS THE USER'S EXPLICIT CALL** ("arrive inside the car for elevators"). `TryGet` is false for a non-`Directional` link, so `DisembarkCell` returns Invalid and the elevator order still aims at the car. The elevator's behaviour is carried by the FALLBACK PATH, not by a special case - so anything that later makes elevators directional would silently change it. - **The route does not divert.** `TryGetTransit` scores candidate pairs partly on the far anchor's distance to the destination, and the front tile is one cell from the link the player clicked, so the intended pair wins by the margin `far.Position` used to win by. - **`CarryNow`'s no-shortcut guard still earns its keep** and must stay: the landing now usually EQUALS `realDest`, which is exactly the shape that once wedged a pawn on a dead pather. It is handled - `StartPath` takes vanilla's already-at-destination branch, fires a real `PatherArrived` through our own prefix (a no-op, record already removed) and the Goto completes - but only because that guard was never re-added. **⚠ THE DEPARTURE SIDE IS UNTOUCHED.** §78c walks the pawn ONTO the mouth so the climb clip starts on the treads; that is not the same question and was not changed. **✅ FIELD-VERIFIED, RUN #397.** The whole journey is in `Player.log`: ``` TRANSIT: Lynch (86,0,257) band 1 -> (69,0,74) band 0 | job=Goto | transit=YES via (71,0,266) -> (71,0,74) TRANSIT: entry cell for AB2_GrandStairsDown 3 at (71,0,266) = (72,0,266) TRANSIT: StartPath rewritten -> (73,0,266) (OnCell) [leg 1 of 2, mouth is (72,0,266)] TRANSIT: LEG2-ON-ARRIVAL Lynch at (73,0,266) -> mouth (72,0,266) TRANSIT: HOLDING Lynch at (72,0,266) for 90t (entry clip) before (71,0,74) TRANSIT: TRANSITED Lynch (71,0,266) -> (69,0,74) (anchor (71,0,74)); resuming to (69,0,74) ``` The far link is at `(71,0,74)` with mouth `(70,0,74)`; the pawn landed on `(69,0,74)` and the job **resumed to that same cell** - off the footprint, journey over. The return leg shows the same shape.
